subject: Kepler renewal: platform proof-of-performance & competitive threat
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@kepler.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Rios <alex.rios@kepler.ai>
Date: 2028-09-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFP window + bakeoff signal for renewal (90-day)

Jordan —

Quick note as we head into renewal: our renewal window opens in October and the execs have asked us to run a short bakeoff for the platform layer. AtlasAI has surfaced as a likely alternative (they pitched an on-prem option + a 20% list discount). Before we get pulled into a full procurement RFP, can you provide a concise performance summary for our current workload (avg p95 latency, throughput at 4k seq, and tail error rates) and the pricing delta for a 2x capacity uplift for 12 months?

High level asks:
- A short performance snapshot we can attach to the procurement packet
- Pricing for reserved capacity (2x) and any temp uplift credits you can offer for proof-of-performance
- SOC2 / security docs we can share with procurement

Appreciate the quick turnaround — procurement expects an internal decision to narrow vendors within two weeks.

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Singh
Head of Platform Ops, Kepler.ai

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@kepler.ai>, Alex Rios <alex.rios@kepler.ai>
Date: 2028-09-10T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: RFP window + bakeoff signal for renewal (90-day)

Ben / Dylan —

FYI: Kepler just signaled a potential bakeoff and wants performance + a 2x uplift price. AtlasAI is bidding on-prem + 20% off — that’s likely the competitive lever. Can you take point on:

1) Ben: prepare a short benchmark one-pager (p95s, throughput 4k sequence, token cost delta) and a clean price sheet for a 12-month reserved uplift. Include three scenarios: conservative (10% uplift), recommended (2x), and aggressive (3x) with breakpoints.

2) Dylan: SOC2/attestation + any compliance attachments (we should redact internal ops notes) — attach the redwood SOC2 summary and a short readme on how Kepler can run a PoP (proof-of-performance) with our dedicated pilot.

I’ll lead the MPO and own the negotiation thread. Keep responses short — procurement wants something to attach in 48 hours.

-Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@kepler.ai>, Alex Rios <alex.rios@kepler.ai>
Date: 2028-09-11T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: RFP window + bakeoff signal for renewal (90-day)

Team / Maya —

Attached is a concise benchmark snapshot and a pricing matrix. High-level takeaways:

- p95 latency (4k seq): 210 ms on current production (95% wafers); AtlasAI reported p95 around 260 ms in 3rd-party notes for a similar stack.
- Sustained throughput: 3.8k tokens/sec per GPU for our quantized instance; with 2x capacity expected to deliver ~7.4k tokens/sec sustained.
- Error rates: 0.4% transient timeouts historically (last 90 days).

Save levers we recommend:
- 3-month proof-of-performance with a 20% uplift credit if Kepler elects Reserved for 12 months thereafter.
- One-time onboarding credit equal to two weeks of reserved consumption to cover migration verification and abbreviated bakeoff costs.
- Dedicated customer success + solutions hours (12 days) included for any reserved uplift >1.5x.

Attached: kepler_benchmark_v2.pdf, pricing_matrix_Kepler.xlsx (sent separately to legal).

Ben Carter
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Attaching the SOC2/attestation summary and a short guide for a controlled PoP run (what logs we’ll need, how to isolate traffic to a dedicated pool, and expected timelines). We can provide a limited-scope on-site review or remote KMS attestation if Kepler procurement requires it — that will need a short SOW.

Attachments included: soc2_readme.pdf (summary), kepler_mop_v1.xlsx (PoP runbook + MOP). Redacted internal notes.

From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@kepler.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Rios <alex.rios@kepler.ai>, procurement@kepler.ai
Date: 2028-09-12T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP window + bakeoff signal for renewal (90-day)

Thanks — this is helpful. A few clarifying points from procurement/exec:

1) AtlasAI’s on‑prem pitch is attractive because our security team wants more control over keys. Would Redwood entertain a hybrid (private control plane + dedicated GPU) pilot for a limited scope?
2) The execs want firm P&L math — your pricing table shows a per-token uplift but we also need a committed monthly spend number and an example invoice/credit treatment if the PoP underperforms.
3) The 20% onboarding credit is good. Procurement wants SLA credit terms spelled out (SLA SLOs, credit percentages, and how credits are applied).

We’re running a short internal decision meeting Friday — can you provide the MOP + pricing + formal SLA language by EOD Thursday? If you can also put the PoP acceptance criteria in writing, that’ll speed things up.

-Maya
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@kepler.ai>, Alex Rios <alex.rios@kepler.ai>, procurement@kepler.ai
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-14T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Kepler mutual action plan & PoP offer (draft)

Maya / Alex / Procurement —

Appreciate the clear asks. Attached is a short Mutual Action Plan (MOP) and a draft offer that addresses the three pillars you raised: security posture, firm committed spend, and PoP acceptance criteria. Key points (summary):

- Hybrid pilot: we will provision a private control plane + dedicated GPU pool for a 2-week PoP. Scope limited to API traffic isolation for the Kepler test tenant; KMS integration via customer-managed keys available under a short SOW.
- Pricing: committed spend examples for a 12-month Reserved capacity (2x) — monthly committed spend shown with breakpoints at 1.5x and 3x. We include a 20% onboarding credit applied as monthly invoice credit over first two months.
- SLA & credits: 99.9% monthly uptime objective for reserved pools; missed SLOs accrue service credits (2% monthly credit per 0.1% below SLO up to 30%). Credits apply as invoice offsets the following billing cycle; specific measurement windows and dispute CIF are in the draft SLO clause.
- PoP acceptance criteria: 1) p95 latency within 15% of baseline during a 72h steady window; 2) throughput sustainment target met for 4k sequence load; 3) error rate <=0.6% over measurement window. If PoP fails, Kepler receives a 30% credit on the first 3 months of reserved spend or a right to renegotiate terms.

Next steps we propose:
- EOD Thursday: sign-off to move to procurement packet (Kepler internal).
- Week 1 post-sign: 2-week PoP (our infra + Kepler keys).
- Week 3: mutual evaluation and contract finalization if PoP passes.

I’ve attached: kepler_mop_v1.xlsx, kepler_benchmark_v2.pdf, soc2_readme.pdf. Happy to jump on a 30-min call with procurement + security to walk through the MOP.

Best,
Jordan Blake
